Every number traces back to the quote it came from.

Ledger is ProcurePilot's design system. Supplier quotes arrive as emails, PDFs and phone photos, in Arabic and English. The interface turns them into one comparable line, with an explicit currency and a visible source, and leaves the purchase decision to a person.

Brand alignment Colours and type follow docs/brand (Converge, adopted 2026-10-14): Navy #0B2545, Teal #12A594, Paper #F4F6F9 and Readex Pro. One documented exception, recorded in docs/brand/README.md: figures in tables and money columns use Noto Kufi Arabic, because Readex Pro has no tabular figures.

Principles

A financial tool used by buyers, owners and branch staff in a busy working day. Calm and precision beat spectacle.

Evidence sits beside the number

Every price, total and saving links to its source: the page, the email, the purchase order. A number with no source is never shown as fact.

PDF page 2

Currency is part of the number

No amount appears without its currency, and the currency is never guessed. When a quote does not state one, the line goes to review with the home currency only as a suggestion.

EGP 1,250.00 ١٬٢٥٠٫٠٠ ج.م.

A double rule marks a verified total

Borrowed from the accounting ledger: a double underline means a total is closed and reconciled. Ledger uses it only for the best offer and for proven savings, so it keeps its meaning.

EGP 284,610.00

A person authorises

Automation prepares and routes; it never buys. Approval buttons name the action, state what happens next, and appear only for people who hold the authority.

Colour

Navy for the brand and for actions, ledger paper for surfaces, and teal reserved for the best offer and money saved, the same job it does in the logo, where the winning bar keeps going as an arrow. Dark mode turns the surfaces navy. Contrast ratios below are computed live from the current token values, so they change when you switch to dark mode.

Primitive ramps

Raw values with no meaning. No component reads them directly; only semantic tokens point at them. Higher numbers are darker.

Three token layers: primitive, semantic, component

Dark mode changes only the semantic layer: the same semantic token points at a different primitive, and the component never changes. Switch the theme to watch the first column move.

Data visualisation

Six category colours led by navy, and a five-step navy ramp. Every category colour clears 3:1 on the card in both themes. Teal is not a category colour, and no category colour sits near it: teal appears in a chart only when the value is money saved.

Typography

One family for both scripts: Readex Pro, drawn for Arabic and Latin together with matched weights, so a mixed-language screen never looks like two fonts arguing. The scale is the classical one, 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 24, 36, 48. Weights are 400 and 500 for text and 600 for headings, as in the wordmark. Large Latin headings are tracked −0.02em; Arabic is never tracked. Arabic gets more line height (1.7 against 1.5). Readex Pro has no tabular figures, so numbers in tables and money columns use Noto Kufi Arabic (tabular Latin and Arabic-Indic digits); everything else stays Readex Pro.

Money formatting, live and following the language

Type an amount. The first column follows the page language; the second is the Arabic variant with Western digits, for tenants who choose it. Negatives use a true minus sign, and the currency is never dropped.

EGP
Arabic-Indic digits are accepted too

Space, shape, elevation and motion

The 4px scale stays. Corner radius grows with the size of the thing: a chip is crisper than a button, a button crisper than a card. Borders separate; shadow is only for things that float above the page.

Radius

chip 3pxStatus chips, citations
control 6pxButtons, fields, menus
card 10pxCards, tables
panel 16pxDialogs, side sheets

Elevation

elev-0Cards and tables: border only
elev-1Sticky bars while scrolling
elev-2Menus, popovers, tooltips
elev-3Dialogs

Motion

Motion answers something a person did: opening, expanding, confirming. The only unprompted motion is the double rule drawing under a verified total, once. When the system asks for reduced motion, every duration token becomes zero.

--pp-dur-fast120ms, ease
Hover, press, focus ring
--pp-dur220ms, ease
Menus, tabs, switches, toasts
--pp-dur-slow360ms, ease
Dialogs and side sheets
--pp-dur-rule900ms, ease
Drawing the double rule, once per page
--pp-ease-exit220ms
Things leaving speed up on the way out

Iconography

Material Symbols Outlined from Google Fonts, because Angular Material already speaks it. Weight 300 at 20 to 24px, so icon strokes sit close to Readex Pro's 400 text. Status-chip glyphs stay custom, because their shape is their meaning.

schedule16px: inline and chips
schedule20px: buttons and menus
schedule24px: top bar and mobile
check_circleFilled: active item only

Mirror in Arabic

Anything that points along the reading direction or means forward and back. Switch the language to watch them flip.

arrow_forwardarrow_forward

chevron_rightchevron_right
sendsend

Never mirror

Real-world objects and universal marks: the tick, the clock, the magnifier, upload and download.

checkcheck
scheduleschedule
searchsearch
downloaddownload
uploadupload
notificationsnotifications
mailmail
deletedelete

An icon is never the only label: every icon-only button carries an accessible name and a tooltip, and decorative icons are hidden from screen readers.

The decision sits under the thumb

Approve and reject live in a fixed bar above the navigation. Approve is wider; reject is outlined in red, not filled.

The total before the detail

Lines, total and the budget left share one card, so a typical request needs no scrolling before the decision.

Same language, same shapes

Status chips keep their shapes; currency and digits follow the device language. In Arabic the back arrow flips and everything else follows the logical order.

48px touch targets

Every button and navigation item is at least 48px, whatever the density.

App shell

A sidebar named by the jobs people do, not by system modules. Counts appear only for work waiting on you. At phone width the sidebar becomes a scrolling row.

Mapping to Angular Material 19

Ledger tokens feed Material 19's system variables, so every Material component follows them without per-component overrides.

Material 19 system tokenLedger tokenUsed by
--mat-sys-primary / on-primary--pp-primary / --pp-on-primaryFlat buttons, focus, selected tabs, checkboxes
--mat-sys-primary-container--pp-primary-containerTonal buttons, selected rows, active nav
--mat-sys-surface--pp-surface-pageSidenav content, page
--mat-sys-surface-container-lowest--pp-surface-cardCards, tables, dialogs
--mat-sys-surface-container-high--pp-surface-sunkenDisabled fills, source panes
--mat-sys-on-surface / on-surface-variant--pp-text-strong / --pp-text-mutedAll text
--mat-sys-outline / outline-variant--pp-border-strong / --pp-borderOutlined fields, dividers
--mat-sys-error / error-container--pp-error / --pp-error-containerField errors, destructive buttons
--mat-sys-tertiary / tertiary-container--pp-savings / --pp-savings-containerSavings and best-offer emphasis
--mat-sys-corner-extra-small / small / medium / largechip / control / card / panelShape
--mat-sys-level1 / level2 / level3--pp-elev-1 / 2 / 3Menus, dialogs
--mat-sys-inverse-surface / inverse-on-surface / inverse-primary--pp-inverse-surface / --pp-on-inverse-surface / --pp-inverse-primarySnackbars, tooltips
mat.theme((typography: …))--pp-fontAll Material typescale roles
.pp-figures on numeric mat-cell / mat-footer-cell, money inputs--pp-font-figuresFigures that must align in columns

Success, warning and info have no Material system role, so they stay as Ledger-only tokens used by status chips and banners. Success is a yellower green than brand teal and info is blue, so an approved chip never reads as money saved.
